chosen.premise: When wounded or tired, Magmar bathes in lava to heal and recover, treating a volcano like a hot spring.
chosen.hook: Magmar’s idea of rest is soaking in lava.
chosen.visualIdea: Show Magmar limping into a volcano, then emerging refreshed from a lava pool labeled “hot spring.”
chosen.note: A uniquely Magmar behavior with a vivid contradiction: lava is both its danger and its recovery treatment. Multiple Pokédex entries directly support both healing wounds and easing fatigue.

candidates.premise: Magmar’s body is always burning, its breath raises the temperature, and a sneeze launches flames.
candidates.hook: For Magmar, sneezing is basically a flamethrower.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate a normal breath warming the air, then cut to an explosive fiery sneeze.
candidates.note: The flaming sneeze is highly surprising and directly supported by Ultra Sun, though the angle combines several related facts rather than centering one especially strong rule.

candidates.premise: Magmar dispatches prey with fire, then regrets it when the flames reduce its intended meal to a charred crisp.
candidates.hook: Magmar can defeat its prey so thoroughly that dinner disappears.
candidates.visualIdea: Follow a hunt from confident fire attack to Magmar staring sadly at an overcooked silhouette.
candidates.note: A sharp, memorable contradiction directly supported by Sword: fire is effective at hunting but can destroy the meal. The visual needs careful framing to avoid becoming merely comedic or grim.

candidates.premise: Magmar’s orange glow lets it hide perfectly among flames, turning its most obvious feature into camouflage.
candidates.hook: Magmar hides by looking exactly like fire.
candidates.visualIdea: Place Magmar inside a wall of flames and slowly reveal that its silhouette was there all along.
candidates.note: The camouflage contradiction is concrete and easy to reveal visually, but the core fact is relatively straightforward and only supported by closely repeated entries.

candidates.premise: Magmar dislikes cold so much that it blasts scorching flames until the surrounding environment suits it.
candidates.hook: Magmar doesn’t escape the cold—it changes the weather.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a freezing landscape transform into a blazing habitat as Magmar exhales flames.
candidates.note: Magmar reshaping its surroundings to escape cold is distinctive and visual, but calling this changing the weather overstates the cited claim, which only says it makes the environment suitable.

candidates.premise: Magmar reaches its final form only through a trade while holding a Magmarizer, not by leveling up.
candidates.hook: Magmar’s final evolution requires someone else to trade it away.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Magmar leveling past 30 unchanged, then a Magmarizer trade triggering its final evolution.
candidates.note: The evolution requirement is precise and supported by the supplied chain, but trade evolutions and Magmortar’s method are familiar to many fans, making the hook less surprising.

rounds.request: N/A—the lava-hot-spring angle is strong enough. Stronger alternatives would need an equally Magmar-specific contradiction, a direct Pokédex-supported rule, and a clearer visual transformation or payoff.
